name: ARDA
tagline: A small consumer AI assistant app that sits between chat and a personal database of your stuff.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a small independent AI assistant product, and we have not verified its exact feature surface or price, so treat the confidence rating as load bearing. The archetype is well understood: a chat layer plus a structured store for notes, tasks, and reminders, wrapped in a phone-shaped interface. An agent can rebuild that core loop locally in a weekend, pointed at any model API, and the result will genuinely hold your data. Where the DIY version falls down is everywhere the product actually earns money: a real mobile app, background sync, push notifications, calendar and mail hookups, and the taste that makes the thing pleasant to open twice a day. Buildable, not equivalent.
coreLoopDIY: Runs a local single-user web app where you talk to a model and it reads and writes your own notes, tasks, and reminders in a SQLite file you own.
requirements: An API key for an OpenAI-compatible model endpoint
Somewhere to keep the process running if you want reminders to actually fire
whatYouLose: A native mobile app, which is where an assistant like this lives or dies
Push notifications and reliable background reminders
Any prebuilt calendar, email, or contacts integrations
Onboarding, polish, and the small interaction details that make daily use stick
Someone else's problem when the model API changes or the sync breaks
moatNotes: Consumer assistant apps compete on feel and on how much of your life you have already poured in, not on anything technically scarce.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a personal assistant is only useful if it is in your pocket, wakes you up at the right moment, and does not require you to remember which port it runs on. Paying a few dollars a month buys a signed mobile binary, notifications that fire, sync between devices, and someone maintaining the model plumbing. The self-hosted version wins on data ownership and on not being at the mercy of a small startup's runway, and it loses on every single one of the ergonomics that make you open the app on a Tuesday morning.
notes: Entry drafted without hands-on use, so the feature list and pricing here are unverified; the verdict is about the category as much as the product.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal AI assistant that runs on my own machine. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, one file at ./data/arda.db, schema created on first run.
- Model calls through an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint. Read OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL and MODEL from .env.local. Write a .env.example, never commit real keys.

Data model:
- notes: id, title, body, tags, created_at, updated_at
- tasks: id, title, notes, due_at nullable, done boolean, created_at
- reminders: id, task_id nullable, text, fire_at, fired boolean
- messages: id, role, content, created_at

Features that are in scope:
- A single chat page. My message goes to the model with tool definitions for create_note, search_notes, create_task, list_tasks, complete_task, create_reminder, list_reminders.
- Implement those tools as server actions that hit SQLite directly. Loop tool calls until the model returns prose. Stream the reply.
- A second page listing notes and tasks with plain forms so I can edit without talking to a model.
- Full text search over notes using SQLite FTS5.
- A /api/tick route that returns due, unfired reminders and marks them fired. Poll it from the client every 60 seconds and show a browser notification if permission is granted.

Out of scope, do not build: auth, multi-user, mobile apps, push notifications, calendar or email integrations, vector search, any hosted deployment config.

Deliver a README with exactly the commands to install, set env vars, and run. Seed the db with three example notes and two tasks so the first launch is not empty.
